Factorization, completing the square, and the quadratic formula are three methods for solving quadratic equations. Quadratic formula can be derived from the method of completing the square. 

The solutions to a quadratic equation correspond to the x-coordinates of the points where the graph of the corresponding quadratic function intersects the x-axis. 

Considering that a quadratic function may or may not intersect the x-axis, we can have 0, 1, or 2 solutions to a quadratic equation. The discriminant of a quadratic equation helps us determine the number of solutions without actually solving the equation.
